+0.30%](/quote/T-PA/ "T-PA")

This article first appeared on [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3156374/why-att-might-be-the-calm-in-the-market-storm?utm_source=yahoo_finance&utm_medium=syndication&utm_campaign=headlines&r=caf6fe0e0db70d936033da5461e60141).

AT&T's ([NYSE:T](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/T)) stock has rallied strongly this year, gaining over 30% before easing off recent highs. The enthusiasm has faded since and the company's latest earnings report disappointed some investors. While the market focused on the negatives, I believe there were several encouraging signs that deserve more attention. AT&T is growing its fiber network at a healthy pace, capturing more converged customers who use both mobile and home broadband, and producing enough free cash flow (FCF) to support its dividend and reduce debt.

In this article, I will break down AT&T's business model, going through its most recent earnings, and provide my own view on whether the stock still represents an attractive investment at this stage.

# **Business and Key Drivers**

AT&T aims to position itself as America's premier converged connectivity provider. The company is unique among major US telecommunications firms because it owns and operates two scaled, complementary infrastructure assets: high-speed 5G wireless and Fiber broadband. Management often says this dual setup gives AT&T a lasting advantage, one that can deliver stronger returns over time by keeping customers tied to the company for both mobile and home connections.

The growth potential here is significant. The [United States broadband services market](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/horizon/outlook/broadband-services-market/united-states) generated around $74 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach roughly $114 billion by 2030, implying a compound annual growth rate of about 7.5%. Wireless is still expected to be the fastest-growing piece of that market as data demand keeps rising, helped by trends like remote work and video streaming. AT&T's answer is to keep pushing on both fronts. Expanding fiber faster while adding more 5G capacity.

Within its core operations, mobility remains the main revenue contributor, making up close to 70% of total sales, or about $21.7 billion in the [third quarter of 2025](https://investors.att.com/~/media/Files/A/ATT-IR-V2/financial-reports/quarterly-earnings/2025/3Q-2025/3Q25_ATT_News_Release.pdf). The company added 405,000 postpaid phone subscribers, bringing its total to just under 74 million; that's a solid number in a mature and highly competitive market, though still well below [T-Mobile's](https://s29.q4cdn.com/310188824/files/doc_financials/2025/q3/Q3-2025-Earnings-Release-vFinal.pdf) ([NASDAQ:TMUS](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TMUS)) 1.0 million postpaid phone adds in the same quarter. Churn ticked up slightly to 0.92% as promotions heated up when more customers reached the end of their phone payment cycles. T-Mobile still leads on growth and retention, but AT&T's focus is less on headline subscriber gains and more on building long-term, higher-value relationships.

Fiber continues to be AT&T's primary growth driver. In the third quarter, fiber subscribers grew by 288,000 to surpass 10 million, with fiber revenue up 17% year over year (YoY). Fiber broadband remains AT&T's most profitable product, carrying EBITDA margins that could eventually approach 50% at scale. Once deployed, fiber becomes a lasting infrastructure advantage. It offers more speed, reliability, and capacity, which over time gives AT&T a real edge in customer retention and economics. The network now passes [31 million locations](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/T), with a goal of reaching 60 million by 2030. AT&T has also been active in M&A, through its Gigapower joint venture and the planned acquisition of [Lumen's Mass Markets](https://about.att.com/story/2025/lumen-mass-markets-fiber-business.html) fiber business.

Fixed Wireless Access (FWA), sold under AT&T Internet Air, complements the fiber rollout. The company's focus on 5G capacity was underscored by the [$23 billion acquisition](https://about.att.com/story/2025/echostar.html) of spectrum licenses from EchoStar. The service is now available in parts of 47 states and added 270,000 FWA subscribers in Q3, doubling from the prior year. The strategy is to use FWA to win broadband customers now and eventually migrate them to fiber when fiber builds catch up. This strategy helps AT&T grow its broadband presence today while keeping a clear path toward faster and more profitable connections in the future.

Another thing that sets AT&T apart is that it owns most of the infrastructure it depends on. Because it controls both the fiber network and the wireless side, the company can manage costs more directly, maintain consistent service quality, and package its offerings in ways that rivals often struggle to match.

Management has reiterated that customers who take both fiber and wireless plans have the lowest churn profile and generate the highest lifetime values. By the end of Q3 2025, about 42% of AT&T Fiber households also had an AT&T Mobility line, up 180 basis points (bps) from a year earlier. The company also operates FirstNet, the nationwide first-responder network built under a 25-year government contract. FirstNet now supports over 7.8 million lines and continues to expand coverage using federally supported capital. No competitor has that deal.

The U.S. telecom market remains competitive, but its scale leaves room for multiple winners. The USA has roughly 132 million households, and AT&T serves about 13.5 million broadband customers today, including more than 10 million on fiber. In wireless, it ranks third by total postpaid phone subscribers, behind Verizon ([NYSE:VZ](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/VZ)) and T-Mobile, yet continues to close the gap. I view this market less as a zero-sum battle and more as a durable triopoly, where each player can succeed within its strategic lane.

# **Financials**

AT&T's [third-quarter](https://investors.att.com/~/media/Files/A/ATT-IR-V2/financial-reports/quarterly-earnings/2025/3Q-2025/3Q25_ATT_News_Release.pdf) results came in slightly below Wall Street expectations but confirmed steady operational progress. Revenue reached $30.7 billion, just shy of the $30.8 billion consensus estimate, representing 2% YoY growth. Mobility grew 3%, Consumer Wireline rose 6%, while Business Wireline slipped 8%. Adjusted EBITDA reached $11.9 billion, with margins improving slightly to 38.6%. That uptick came mostly from higher fiber contribution and ongoing savings from shutting down older copper-based networks.

Average revenue per postpaid phone user (ARPU) was $56.64, down less than 1% year over year. That small decline hides two opposing dynamics. On one hand, customers are upgrading to higher-priced unlimited plans that include more data and perks, which pushes ARPU up. On the other, AT&T has leaned into multi-line discounts, senior plans, and bundle offers that pull the average back down. Management said these mix effects are intentional. They aim to lift household-level revenue and keep customers for longer. The trade-off is that ARPU may look flat in the short term, even as overall customer value improves.

Free cash flow for the quarter totaled $4.9 billion, bringing year-to-date FCF to $12.4 billion. Management reaffirmed its full-year target of at least $16 billion. The annual dividend, roughly $8 billion, is well covered, leaving room to reduce debt and even buybacks. The payout of $1.11 per share yields about 4.4% and continues to be funded entirely from operations rather than borrowing.

Capital expenditures came in at $4.9 billion for the quarter and are expected to reach between $22 billion and $22.5 billion for the full year. Most of this investment is going into fiber expansion and 5G network upgrades, including mid-band spectrum builds that improve coverage and capacity. At the same time, AT&T is accelerating the retirement of legacy copper infrastructure, which should cut maintenance costs and make the network far more efficient over time. Management still sees 2025 as the peak year for heavy investment, with spending expected to ease once the main phases of fiber and 5G construction are behind it.

AT&T's balance sheet is in its best shape in years. At the end of 2022, the company held $136 billion in debt and just $3.7 billion in cash, which equated to a net leverage ratio of around 3.2x EBITDA. By the end of the third quarter of 2025, total debt was roughly unchanged at $139 billion, but cash had risen to more than $20 billion, bringing net leverage down to 2.6x. That ratio will temporarily rise in 2026 when the $23 billion EchoStar spectrum acquisition closes, but management has reaffirmed its goal of returning to 2.5x within three years.

Reaching that target will require continued discipline. Much of the $1618 billion in expected annual free cash flow will likely be directed toward deleveraging rather than larger shareholder distributions. Still, AT&T opted to maintain its $4 billion buyback program under the 2024 authorization, a move that has drawn mixed reactions from investors given the near-term debt load.

At the bottom line, profitability has stabilized following years of restructuring. GAAP net income for the quarter was $9.3 billion, though that figure includes a one-time gain from the sale of AT&T's remaining 70% stake in DirecTV. Adjusted net income was $3.9 billion, or $0.54 per share, essentially flat compared with the same quarter last year.

# **Valuation**

Given AT&T's asset-heavy and transitional business model, valuation should primarily reflect the quality of its infrastructure. Enterprise value provides the clearest picture, though traditional multiples still offer useful context.

Source: Gurufocus

The stock trades around 12x forward earnings (P/E) and 6x enterprise value to EBITDA, compared with a five-year average closer to 7.8x. At first glance, that might look like a modest undervaluation, but it also suggests that the market is partially pricing in the additional debt from the EchoStar acquisition. On the other hand, the forward price-to-sales ratio has expanded to about 1.4x, slightly above its five-year average, showing that investors are becoming more comfortable with AT&T's financial trajectory. The FCF yield also adds some margin of safety, with the trailing twelve-month figure around 9%.

Source: Author

Peer comparisons make the valuation context clearer. Verizon trades near 8x forward earnings and 6x EV/EBITDA. Its growth profile is similar to AT&T, but Verizon still remains the [quality leader](https://www.verizon.com/about/news/verizon-remains-americas-best-wireless-network) in network reliability and offers the higher dividend yield, which makes the stock appear undervalued relative to AT&T. T-Mobile, meanwhile, trades at more than 20x forward P/E and 10x EV/EBITDA, reflecting faster growth and lower capital intensity.

Source: Author

Looking at unit economics adds another layer of insight. AT&T's enterprise value per wireless subscriber is roughly $2,800, compared to $2,300 for Verizon and $2,600 for T-Mobile. On this basis, AT&T and T-Mobile are valued relatively closely per connection, with Verizon trading at a discount (Verizon's figures are based on Q2 2025 results, while AT&T and T-Mobile reflect Q3 2025 data, which may slightly skew the comparison).

Another useful way to look at it is free cash flow per subscriber, and here AT&T stands out. The company generates roughly $170 in annual FCF per user, ahead of Verizon at about $140 and T-Mobile at just under $120. Despite having fewer total subscribers, AT&T extracts more FCF per user. Although Verizon looks cheaper based on traditional valuation metrics, and T-Mobile trades at higher multiples thanks to its faster growth, AT&T's stronger cash generation per customer helps justify why it sits in the middle and why the market gives it a slight premium per subscriber.

The stock no longer represents a deep-value investment, but it does offer a combination of income, stability, and moderate growth that remains attractive to long-term investors in my opinion.

# **Risks**

AT&T's greatest risk is execution. The company's convergence strategy depends on simultaneously expanding fiber, managing wireless churn, and reducing leverage. Each of those tasks requires capital, discipline, and flawless coordination. Missing on any front could slow the whole plan.

Competition remains intense, particularly from T-Mobile, which continues to lead the industry with around one million postpaid phone additions in the third quarter alone. To keep its base, AT&T has to balance promotions with margin protection.

The fiber expansion also comes with its own challenges. Reaching 60 million homes by 2030 is an ambitious target, and plenty can get in the way, such as permitting delays, labor shortages, and rising construction costs. Even if the rollout stays on track, success ultimately depends on take rates in new markets to justify the investment.

Finally, capital allocation remains under scrutiny. Repurchasing shares while adding $23 billion of debt is aggressive. It signals confidence, but it also narrows the margin of financial safety at a time when deleveraging should be the priority. If free cash flow were to disappoint, investors could start to be concerned about the sustainability of dividends.

# **My Final Take**

AT&T today is a disciplined, capital-intensive infrastructure story. It's a multi-year investment in the belief that pairing 5G and fiber creates a durable, cash-generating competitive moat.

Yet competition across the big three remains fierce, but this is not a zero-sum game. Verizon, T-Mobile, and AT&T each occupy a distinct lane within what has effectively become a triopoly. AT&T's advantage lies in its convergence model and balance between growth and income. The company now needs to prove it can grow, deleverage, and invest, all at once.

In my view, AT&T's story is in great shape. Wireless additions remain steady. Fiber is scaling profitably. Margins are expanding, and FCF generation is consistent. The dividend is covered. At roughly 12x earnings and a 4.4% yield, AT&T appears fairly valued for what it offers. It offers steady income, moderate upside, and stability in a market increasingly driven by speculation.

For investors growing cautious about potential bubbles forming in the broader market or certain sectors, AT&T could be a sensible stock to add for stability and income.

Shares have added about 3.7% in that time frame, outperforming the S&P 500.\\n\\nWill the recent positive trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is AT&T due for a pullback? Well, first let's take a quick look at its latest earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent catalysts for AT&T Inc. before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.\\n\\n**T Misses Q3 Earnings & Revenue Estimates Despite Healthy Demand**\\n\\nAT&T reported\u00a0modest third-quarter 2025 results with healthy mobility and broadband demand trends. However, both adjusted earnings and revenues missed the respective Zacks Consensus Estimate.  \\n  \\nThe company witnessed solid wireless traction and customer additions, which were partially offset by lower demand for legacy voice and data services. AT&T recorded strong subscriber growth backed by a resilient business model and robust cash flow position, driven by a diligent execution of operational plans. AT&T expects to continue investing in key areas of 5G and fiber and adjust its business according to the evolving market scenario to fuel long-term growth.  \\n  \\n**Net Income**  \\n  \\nOn a GAAP basis, AT&T reported a net income of $9.28 billion or $1.29 per share against a net loss of $0.23 billion or a loss of 3 cents per share in the year-ago quarter. The significant improvement was primarily attributable to a $5.5 billion gain from the sale of DIRECTV investments during the reported quarter and a $4.4 billion non-cash goodwill impairment charge in the year-earlier period.  \\n  \\nExcluding non-recurring items, adjusted earnings remained flat at 54 cents per share. Adjusted earnings for the third quarter missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by a penny.\u00a0  \\n  \\n**Quarter Details**  \\n  \\nQuarterly GAAP operating revenues increased 1.6% year over year to $30.71 billion, largely due to higher Mobility service and equipment sales, Consumer Wireline and Mexico revenues, partially offset by lower Business Wireline revenues. The top line missed the consensus mark of $30.96 billion.\u00a0  \\n  \\nAdjusted operating income increased to $6.55 billion from $6.51 billion for respective adjusted operating income margins of 21.3% and 21.6%. Adjusted EBITDA improved to $11.86 billion from $11.59 billion.  \\n  \\nAT&T witnessed solid subscriber momentum with 328,000 post-paid net additions. This included 405,000 postpaid wireless phone additions. Postpaid churn was 1.07%, while postpaid phone-only average revenue per user (ARPU) decreased 0.8% year over year to $56.64 due to lower international roaming.  \\n  \\n**Segmental Performance**  \\n  \\n**Communications:** Total segment operating revenues were $29.52 billion, up from $29.07 billion, as improvements in the Mobility business (up 3.1% to $21.71 billion) and Consumer Wireline (up 4.1% to $3.56 billion) was partially offset by a decline in Business Wireline (down 7.8% to $4.25 billion). The segment revenues missed our estimates of $30.67 billion.  \\n  \\nService revenues from the Mobility unit improved 2.3% to $16.93 billion, driven by solid subscriber gains, while equipment revenues were up 6.1% year over year to $4.79 billion due to higher volumes of non-phone sales and higher-priced phone sales. Revenues from the Consumer Wireline business were up due to a gain in fiber broadband. AT&T recorded net fiber additions of 288,000, while Internet Air added 270,000 subscribers during the quarter. By the end of 2030, AT&T expects to reach approximately 50 million customer locations with its in-region fiber network and more than 60 million fiber locations when including the Lumen Mass Markets fiber assets.  \\n  \\nRevenues from Business Wireline were down due to lower demand for legacy voice and data services as customers shifted to more advanced IP-based offerings. Total segment operating income declined 0.8% to $7.1 billion, with operating margins of 24% (down 60 bps). Adjusted EBITDA was $12.17 billion compared with $11.97 billion in the year-ago quarter.  \\n  \\n**Latin America:** Total operating revenues were $1.09 billion, up 7.1% year over year, due to higher equipment sales and service revenues. Adjusted EBITDA improved to $199 million from $168 million in the year-ago quarter.  \\n  \\n**Cash Flow & Liquidity**  \\n  \\nFor the first nine months of 2025, AT&T generated $28.96 billion of cash from operations compared with $26.87 billion a year ago. Finance\\n\\n [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/)\\n\\n[Mail](https://mail.yahoo.com/)\\n\\n[Sign in](https://login.yahoo.com/?.lang=en-US&src=finance)\\n\\n# Why AT&T Might Be the Calm in the Market Storm\\n\\nRenato Neves, CFA\\n\\n12 min read\\n\\nIn this article:  \\n\\n[T\\n\\n-1.20%](/quote/T/ \\\"T\\\")\\n\\n[T-PA\\n\\n+0.30%](/quote/T-PA/ \\\"T-PA\\\")\\n\\nThis article first appeared on [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3156374/why-att-might-be-the-calm-in-the-market-storm?utm_source=yahoo_finance&utm_medium=syndication&utm_campaign=headlines&r=caf6fe0e0db70d936033da5461e60141).\\n\\nAT&T's ([NYSE:T](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/T)) stock has rallied strongly this year, gaining over 30% before easing off recent highs. The enthusiasm has faded since and the company's latest earnings report disappointed some investors. While the market focused on the negatives, I believe there were several encouraging signs that deserve more attention. AT&T is growing its fiber network at a healthy pace, capturing more converged customers who use both mobile and home broadband, and producing enough free cash flow (FCF) to support its dividend and reduce debt.\\n\\nIn this article, I will break down AT&T's business model, going through its most recent earnings, and provide my own view on whether the stock still represents an attractive investment at this stage.\\n\\n# **Business and Key Drivers**\\n\\nAT&T aims to position itself as America's premier converged connectivity provider. The company is unique among major US telecommunications firms because it owns and operates two scaled, complementary infrastructure assets: high-speed 5G wireless and Fiber broadband. Management often says this dual setup gives AT&T a lasting advantage, one that can deliver stronger returns over time by keeping customers tied to the company for both mobile and home connections.\\n\\nThe growth potential here is significant. The [United States broadband services market](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/horizon/outlook/broadband-services-market/united-states) generated around $74 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach roughly $114 billion by 2030, implying a compound annual growth rate of about 7.5%. Wireless is still expected to be the fastest-growing piece of that market as data demand keeps rising, helped by trends like remote work and video streaming. AT&T's answer is to keep pushing on both fronts. Expanding fiber faster while adding more 5G capacity.\\n\\nWithin its core operations, mobility remains the main revenue contributor, making up close to 70% of total sales, or about $21.7 billion in the [third quarter of 2025](https://investors.att.com/~/media/Files/A/ATT-IR-V2/financial-reports/quarterly-earnings/2025/3Q-2025/3Q25_ATT_News_Release.pdf). The company added 405,000 postpaid phone subscribers, bringing its total to just under 74 million; that's a solid number in a mature and highly competitive market, though still well below [T-Mobile's](https://s29.q4cdn.com/310188824/files/doc_financials/2025/q3/Q3-2025-Earnings-Release-vFinal.pdf) ([NASDAQ:TMUS](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TMUS)) 1.0 million postpaid phone adds in the same quarter. Churn ticked up slightly to 0.92% as promotions heated up when more customers reached the end of their phone payment cycles. T-Mobile still leads on growth and retention, but AT&T's focus is less on headline subscriber gains and more on building long-term, higher-value relationships.\\n\\nFiber continues to be AT&T's primary growth driver. In the third quarter, fiber subscribers grew by 288,000 to surpass 10 million, with fiber revenue up 17% year over year (YoY). Fiber broadband remains AT&T's most profitable product, carrying EBITDA margins that could eventually approach 50% at scale. Once deployed, fiber becomes a lasting infrastructure advantage. It offers more speed, reliability, and capacity, which over time gives AT&T a real edge in customer retention and economics. The network now passes [31 million locations](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/T), with a goal of reaching 60 million by 2030. AT&T has also been active in M&A, through its Gigapower joint venture and the planned acquisition of [Lumen's Mass Markets](https://about.att.com/story/2025/lumen-mass-markets-fiber-business.html) fiber business.\\n\\nFixed Wireless Access (FWA), sold under AT&T Internet Air, complements the fiber rollout. The company's focus on 5G capacity was underscored by the [$23 billion acquisition](https://about.att.com/story/2025/echostar.html) of spectrum licenses from EchoStar. The service is now available in parts of 47 states and added 270,000 FWA subscribers in Q3, doubling from the prior year. The strategy is to use FWA to win broadband customers now and eventually migrate them to fiber when fiber builds catch up. This strategy helps AT&T grow its broadband presence today while keeping a clear path toward faster and more profitable connections in the future.\\n\\nAnother thing that sets AT&T apart is that it owns most of the infrastructure it depends on. Because it controls both the fiber network and the wireless side, the company can manage costs more directly, maintain consistent service quality, and package its offerings in ways that rivals often struggle to match.\\n\\nManagement has reiterated that customers who take both fiber and wireless plans have the lowest churn profile and generate the highest lifetime values. By the end of Q3 2025, about 42% of AT&T Fiber households also had an AT&T Mobility line, up 180 basis points (bps) from a year earlier. The company also operates FirstNet, the nationwide first-responder network built under a 25-year government contract. FirstNet now supports over 7.8 million lines and continues to expand coverage using federally supported capital. No competitor has that deal.\\n\\nThe U.S. telecom market remains competitive, but its scale leaves room for multiple winners. The USA has roughly 132 million households, and AT&T serves about 13.5 million broadband customers today, including more than 10 million on fiber. In wireless, it ranks third by total postpaid phone subscribers, behind Verizon ([NYSE:VZ](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/VZ)) and T-Mobile, yet continues to close the gap. I view this market less as a zero-sum battle and more as a durable triopoly, where each player can succeed within its strategic lane.\\n\\n# **Financials**\\n\\nAT&T's [third-quarter](https://investors.att.com/~/media/Files/A/ATT-IR-V2/financial-reports/quarterly-earnings/2025/3Q-2025/3Q25_ATT_News_Release.pdf) results came in slightly below Wall Street expectations but confirmed steady operational progress. Revenue reached $30.7 billion, just shy of the $30.8 billion consensus estimate, representing 2% YoY growth. Mobility grew 3%, Consumer Wireline rose 6%, while Business Wireline slipped 8%. Adjusted EBITDA reached $11.9 billion, with margins improving slightly to 38.6%. That uptick came mostly from higher fiber contribution and ongoing savings from shutting down older copper-based networks.\\n\\nAverage revenue per postpaid phone user (ARPU) was $56.64, down less than 1% year over year. That small decline hides two opposing dynamics. On one hand, customers are upgrading to higher-priced unlimited plans that include more data and perks, which pushes ARPU up. On the other, AT&T has leaned into multi-line discounts, senior plans, and bundle offers that pull the average back down. Management said these mix effects are intentional. They aim to lift household-level revenue and keep customers for longer. The trade-off is that ARPU may look flat in the short term, even as overall customer value improves.\\n\\nFree cash flow for the quarter totaled $4.9 billion, bringing year-to-date FCF to $12.4 billion. Management reaffirmed its full-year target of at least $16 billion. The annual dividend, roughly $8 billion, is well covered, leaving room to reduce debt and even buybacks. The payout of $1.11 per share yields about 4.4% and continues to be funded entirely from operations rather than borrowing.\\n\\nCapital expenditures came in at $4.9 billion for the quarter and are expected to reach between $22 billion and $22.5 billion for the full year. Most of this investment is going into fiber expansion and 5G network upgrades, including mid-band spectrum builds that improve coverage and capacity. At the same time, AT&T is accelerating the retirement of legacy copper infrastructure, which should cut maintenance costs and make the network far more efficient over time. Management still sees 2025 as the peak year for heavy investment, with spending expected to ease once the main phases of fiber and 5G construction are behind it.\\n\\nAT&T's balance sheet is in its best shape in years. At the end of 2022, the company held $136 billion in debt and just $3.7 billion in cash, which equated to a net leverage ratio of around 3.2x EBITDA. By the end of the third quarter of 2025, total debt was roughly unchanged at $139 billion, but cash had risen to more than $20 billion, bringing net leverage down to 2.6x. That ratio will temporarily rise in 2026 when the $23 billion EchoStar spectrum acquisition closes, but management has reaffirmed its goal of returning to 2.5x within three years.\\n\\nReaching that target will require continued discipline. Much of the $1618 billion in expected annual free cash flow will likely be directed toward deleveraging rather than larger shareholder distributions. Still, AT&T opted to maintain its $4 billion buyback program under the 2024 authorization, a move that has drawn mixed reactions from investors given the near-term debt load.\\n\\nAt the bottom line, profitability has stabilized following years of restructuring. GAAP net income for the quarter was $9.3 billion, though that figure includes a one-time gain from the sale of AT&T's remaining 70% stake in DirecTV. Adjusted net income was $3.9 billion, or $0.54 per share, essentially flat compared with the same quarter last year.\\n\\n# **Valuation**\\n\\nGiven AT&T's asset-heavy and transitional business model, valuation should primarily reflect the quality of its infrastructure. Enterprise value provides the clearest picture, though traditional multiples still offer useful context.\\n\\nSource: Gurufocus\\n\\nThe stock trades around 12x forward earnings (P/E) and 6x enterprise value to EBITDA, compared with a five-year average closer to 7.8x. At first glance, that might look like a modest undervaluation, but it also suggests that the market is partially pricing in the additional debt from the EchoStar acquisition. On the other hand, the forward price-to-sales ratio has expanded to about 1.4x, slightly above its five-year average, showing that investors are becoming more comfortable with AT&T's financial trajectory. Verizon trades near 8x forward earnings and 6x EV/EBITDA. Its growth profile is similar to AT&T, but Verizon still remains the [quality leader](https://www.verizon.com/about/news/verizon-remains-americas-best-wireless-network) in network reliability and offers the higher dividend yield, which makes the stock appear undervalued relative to AT&T. T-Mobile, meanwhile, trades at more than 20x forward P/E and 10x EV/EBITDA, reflecting faster growth and lower capital intensity.\\n\\nSource: Author\\n\\nLooking at unit economics adds another layer of insight. AT&T's enterprise value per wireless subscriber is roughly $2,800, compared to $2,300 for Verizon and $2,600 for T-Mobile. # AT&T (T) Up 3.7% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?

Zacks Equity Research

6 min read

In this article:

[T

-1.20%](/quote/T/ "T")

[T-PA

+0.30%](/quote/T-PA/ "T-PA")

[^SPX

+1.55%](/quote/%5ESPX/ "^SPX")

A month has gone by since the last earnings report for AT&T (T). Shares have added about 3.7% in that time frame, outperforming the S&P 500.

Will the recent positive trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is AT&T due for a pullback? Well, first let's take a quick look at its latest earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent catalysts for AT&T Inc. before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.

**T Misses Q3 Earnings & Revenue Estimates Despite Healthy Demand**

AT&T reported modest third-quarter 2025 results with healthy mobility and broadband demand trends. However, both adjusted earnings and revenues missed the respective Zacks Consensus Estimate.  
  
The company witnessed solid wireless traction and customer additions, which were partially offset by lower demand for legacy voice and data services. AT&T recorded strong subscriber growth backed by a resilient business model and robust cash flow position, driven by a diligent execution of operational plans. AT&T expects to continue investing in key areas of 5G and fiber and adjust its business according to the evolving market scenario to fuel long-term growth.  
  
**Net Income**  
  
On a GAAP basis, AT&T reported a net income of $9.28 billion or $1.29 per share against a net loss of $0.23 billion or a loss of 3 cents per share in the year-ago quarter. The significant improvement was primarily attributable to a $5.5 billion gain from the sale of DIRECTV investments during the reported quarter and a $4.4 billion non-cash goodwill impairment charge in the year-earlier period.  
  
Excluding non-recurring items, adjusted earnings remained flat at 54 cents per share. Adjusted earnings for the third quarter missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by a penny.   
  
**Quarter Details**  
  
Quarterly GAAP operating revenues increased 1.6% year over year to $30.71 billion, largely due to higher Mobility service and equipment sales, Consumer Wireline and Mexico revenues, partially offset by lower Business Wireline revenues. The top line missed the consensus mark of $30.96 billion.   
  
Adjusted operating income increased to $6.55 billion from $6.51 billion for respective adjusted operating income margins of 21.3% and 21.6%. Adjusted EBITDA improved to $11.86 billion from $11.59 billion.  
  
AT&T witnessed solid subscriber momentum with 328,000 post-paid net additions. This included 405,000 postpaid wireless phone additions. Postpaid churn was 1.07%, while postpaid phone-only average revenue per user (ARPU) decreased 0.8% year over year to $56.64 due to lower international roaming.  
  
**Segmental Performance**  
  
**Communications:** Total segment operating revenues were $29.52 billion, up from $29.07 billion, as improvements in the Mobility business (up 3.1% to $21.71 billion) and Consumer Wireline (up 4.1% to $3.56 billion) was partially offset by a decline in Business Wireline (down 7.8% to $4.25 billion). The segment revenues missed our estimates of $30.67 billion.  
  
Service revenues from the Mobility unit improved 2.3% to $16.93 billion, driven by solid subscriber gains, while equipment revenues were up 6.1% year over year to $4.79 billion due to higher volumes of non-phone sales and higher-priced phone sales. Revenues from the Consumer Wireline business were up due to a gain in fiber broadband. AT&T recorded net fiber additions of 288,000, while Internet Air added 270,000 subscribers during the quarter. By the end of 2030, AT&T expects to reach approximately 50 million customer locations with its in-region fiber network and more than 60 million fiber locations when including the Lumen Mass Markets fiber assets.  
  
Revenues from Business Wireline were down due to lower demand for legacy voice and data services as customers shifted to more advanced IP-based offerings. Total segment operating income declined 0.8% to $7.1 billion, with operating margins of 24% (down 60 bps). Adjusted EBITDA was $12.17 billion compared with $11.97 billion in the year-ago quarter.  
  
**Latin America:** Total operating revenues were $1.09 billion, up 7.1% year over year, due to higher equipment sales and service revenues. Adjusted EBITDA improved to $199 million from $168 million in the year-ago quarter.  
  
**Cash Flow & Liquidity**  
  
For the first nine months of 2025, AT&T generated $28.96 billion of cash from operations compared with $26.87 billion a year ago. Free cash flow for the quarter was $4.86 billion compared with $4.6 billion in the year-ago quarter. As of Sept. 30, 2025, AT&T had $20.27 billion of cash and cash equivalents with long-term debt of $128.09 billion. The company repurchased $1.5 billion worth of shares during the quarter. Net debt to adjusted EBITDA was about 2.59X.  
  
**Guidance**  
  
While optimizing operations, AT&T is aiming to increase efficiencies to lower operating costs while focusing on 5G and fiber-based connectivity, along with an expanded reach of software-based entertainment platforms. For 2025, AT&T expects wireless service revenues to improve 3% or more, while broadband revenues are anticipated to grow in the mid to high-teens.  
  
Adjusted earnings are projected to be between $1.97 and $2.07 per share. Free cash flow in 2025 is expected to be more than $16 billion due to cost savings. AT&T expects to repurchase $4 billion worth of shares in 2025. The company is also aiming to reduce its debt burden by monetizing non-core assets.

## How Have Estimates Been Moving Since Then?

It turns out, estimates revision have trended upward during the past month.

The consensus estimate has shifted 6.83% due to these changes.

## VGM Scores

At this time, AT&T has a subpar Growth Score of D, though it is lagging a bit on the Momentum Score front with an F. However, the stock has a score of A on the value side, putting it in the top 20% for this investment strategy.

Overall, the stock has an aggregate VGM Score of C. If you aren't focused on one strategy, this score is the one you should be interested in.

## Outlook

Estimates have been broadly trending upward for the stock, and the magnitude of these revisions looks promising. Interestingly, AT&T has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). We expect an in-line return from the stock in the next few months.

# Why AT&T Might Be the Calm in the Market Storm

Renato Neves, CFA

12 min read

In this article:  

[T

-1.20%](/quote/T/ "T")

[T-PA

+0.30%](/quote/T-PA/ "T-PA")

This article first appeared on [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3156374/why-att-might-be-the-calm-in-the-market-storm?utm_source=yahoo_finance&utm_medium=syndication&utm_campaign=headlines&r=caf6fe0e0db70d936033da5461e60141).

AT&T's ([NYSE:T](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/T)) stock has rallied strongly this year, gaining over 30% before easing off recent highs. The enthusiasm has faded since and the company's latest earnings report disappointed some investors. While the market focused on the negatives, I believe there were several encouraging signs that deserve more attention. AT&T is growing its fiber network at a healthy pace, capturing more converged customers who use both mobile and home broadband, and producing enough free cash flow (FCF) to support its dividend and reduce debt.

In this article, I will break down AT&T's business model, going through its most recent earnings, and provide my own view on whether the stock still represents an attractive investment at this stage.

# **Business and Key Drivers**

AT&T aims to position itself as America's premier converged connectivity provider. The company is unique among major US telecommunications firms because it owns and operates two scaled, complementary infrastructure assets: high-speed 5G wireless and Fiber broadband. Management often says this dual setup gives AT&T a lasting advantage, one that can deliver stronger returns over time by keeping customers tied to the company for both mobile and home connections.

The growth potential here is significant. The [United States broadband services market](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/horizon/outlook/broadband-services-market/united-states) generated around $74 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach roughly $114 billion by 2030, implying a compound annual growth rate of about 7.5%. Wireless is still expected to be the fastest-growing piece of that market as data demand keeps rising, helped by trends like remote work and video streaming. AT&T's answer is to keep pushing on both fronts. Expanding fiber faster while adding more 5G capacity.

Within its core operations, mobility remains the main revenue contributor, making up close to 70% of total sales, or about $21.7 billion in the [third quarter of 2025](https://investors.att.com/~/media/Files/A/ATT-IR-V2/financial-reports/quarterly-earnings/2025/3Q-2025/3Q25_ATT_News_Release.pdf). The company added 405,000 postpaid phone subscribers, bringing its total to just under 74 million; that's a solid number in a mature and highly competitive market, though still well below [T-Mobile's](https://s29.q4cdn.com/310188824/files/doc_financials/2025/q3/Q3-2025-Earnings-Release-vFinal.pdf) ([NASDAQ:TMUS](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TMUS)) 1.0 million postpaid phone adds in the same quarter. Churn ticked up slightly to 0.92% as promotions heated up when more customers reached the end of their phone payment cycles. T-Mobile still leads on growth and retention, but AT&T's focus is less on headline subscriber gains and more on building long-term, higher-value relationships.

Fiber continues to be AT&T's primary growth driver. In the third quarter, fiber subscribers grew by 288,000 to surpass 10 million, with fiber revenue up 17% year over year (YoY). Fiber broadband remains AT&T's most profitable product, carrying EBITDA margins that could eventually approach 50% at scale. Once deployed, fiber becomes a lasting infrastructure advantage. It offers more speed, reliability, and capacity, which over time gives AT&T a real edge in customer retention and economics. The network now passes [31 million locations](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/T), with a goal of reaching 60 million by 2030. AT&T has also been active in M&A, through its Gigapower joint venture and the planned acquisition of [Lumen's Mass Markets](https://about.att.com/story/2025/lumen-mass-markets-fiber-business.html) fiber business.

Fixed Wireless Access (FWA), sold under AT&T Internet Air, complements the fiber rollout. The company's focus on 5G capacity was underscored by the [$23 billion acquisition](https://about.att.com/story/2025/echostar.html) of spectrum licenses from EchoStar. The service is now available in parts of 47 states and added 270,000 FWA subscribers in Q3, doubling from the prior year. The strategy is to use FWA to win broadband customers now and eventually migrate them to fiber when fiber builds catch up. This strategy helps AT&T grow its broadband presence today while keeping a clear path toward faster and more profitable connections in the future.

Another thing that sets AT&T apart is that it owns most of the infrastructure it depends on. Because it controls both the fiber network and the wireless side, the company can manage costs more directly, maintain consistent service quality, and package its offerings in ways that rivals often struggle to match.

Management has reiterated that customers who take both fiber and wireless plans have the lowest churn profile and generate the highest lifetime values. By the end of Q3 2025, about 42% of AT&T Fiber households also had an AT&T Mobility line, up 180 basis points (bps) from a year earlier. The company also operates FirstNet, the nationwide first-responder network built under a 25-year government contract. FirstNet now supports over 7.8 million lines and continues to expand coverage using federally supported capital. No competitor has that deal.

The U.S. telecom market remains competitive, but its scale leaves room for multiple winners. The USA has roughly 132 million households, and AT&T serves about 13.5 million broadband customers today, including more than 10 million on fiber. In wireless, it ranks third by total postpaid phone subscribers, behind Verizon ([NYSE:VZ](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/VZ)) and T-Mobile, yet continues to close the gap. I view this market less as a zero-sum battle and more as a durable triopoly, where each player can succeed within its strategic lane.

# **Financials**

AT&T's [third-quarter](https://investors.att.com/~/media/Files/A/ATT-IR-V2/financial-reports/quarterly-earnings/2025/3Q-2025/3Q25_ATT_News_Release.pdf) results came in slightly below Wall Street expectations but confirmed steady operational progress. Revenue reached $30.7 billion, just shy of the $30.8 billion consensus estimate, representing 2% YoY growth. Mobility grew 3%, Consumer Wireline rose 6%, while Business Wireline slipped 8%. Adjusted EBITDA reached $11.9 billion, with margins improving slightly to 38.6%. That uptick came mostly from higher fiber contribution and ongoing savings from shutting down older copper-based networks.

Average revenue per postpaid phone user (ARPU) was $56.64, down less than 1% year over year. That small decline hides two opposing dynamics. On one hand, customers are upgrading to higher-priced unlimited plans that include more data and perks, which pushes ARPU up. On the other, AT&T has leaned into multi-line discounts, senior plans, and bundle offers that pull the average back down. Management said these mix effects are intentional. They aim to lift household-level revenue and keep customers for longer. The trade-off is that ARPU may look flat in the short term, even as overall customer value improves.

Free cash flow for the quarter totaled $4.9 billion, bringing year-to-date FCF to $12.4 billion. Management reaffirmed its full-year target of at least $16 billion. The annual dividend, roughly $8 billion, is well covered, leaving room to reduce debt and even buybacks. The payout of $1.11 per share yields about 4.4% and continues to be funded entirely from operations rather than borrowing.

Capital expenditures came in at $4.9 billion for the quarter and are expected to reach between $22 billion and $22.5 billion for the full year. Most of this investment is going into fiber expansion and 5G network upgrades, including mid-band spectrum builds that improve coverage and capacity. At the same time, AT&T is accelerating the retirement of legacy copper infrastructure, which should cut maintenance costs and make the network far more efficient over time. Management still sees 2025 as the peak year for heavy investment, with spending expected to ease once the main phases of fiber and 5G construction are behind it.

AT&T's balance sheet is in its best shape in years. At the end of 2022, the company held $136 billion in debt and just $3.7 billion in cash, which equated to a net leverage ratio of around 3.2x EBITDA. By the end of the third quarter of 2025, total debt was roughly unchanged at $139 billion, but cash had risen to more than $20 billion, bringing net leverage down to 2.6x. That ratio will temporarily rise in 2026 when the $23 billion EchoStar spectrum acquisition closes, but management has reaffirmed its goal of returning to 2.5x within three years.

Reaching that target will require continued discipline. Much of the $1618 billion in expected annual free cash flow will likely be directed toward deleveraging rather than larger shareholder distributions. Still, AT&T opted to maintain its $4 billion buyback program under the 2024 authorization, a move that has drawn mixed reactions from investors given the near-term debt load.

At the bottom line, profitability has stabilized following years of restructuring. GAAP net income for the quarter was $9.3 billion, though that figure includes a one-time gain from the sale of AT&T's remaining 70% stake in DirecTV. Adjusted net income was $3.9 billion, or $0.54 per share, essentially flat compared with the same quarter last year.

# **Valuation**

Given AT&T's asset-heavy and transitional business model, valuation should primarily reflect the quality of its infrastructure. Enterprise value provides the clearest picture, though traditional multiples still offer useful context.

Source: Gurufocus

The stock trades around 12x forward earnings (P/E) and 6x enterprise value to EBITDA, compared with a five-year average closer to 7.8x. At first glance, that might look like a modest undervaluation, but it also suggests that the market is partially pricing in the additional debt from the EchoStar acquisition. On the other hand, the forward price-to-sales ratio has expanded to about 1.4x, slightly above its five-year average, showing that investors are becoming more comfortable with AT&T's financial trajectory. The FCF yield also adds some margin of safety, with the trailing twelve-month figure around 9%.

Source: Author

Peer comparisons make the valuation context clearer. Verizon trades near 8x forward earnings and 6x EV/EBITDA. Its growth profile is similar to AT&T, but Verizon still remains the [quality leader](https://www.verizon.com/about/news/verizon-remains-americas-best-wireless-network) in network reliability and offers the higher dividend yield, which makes the stock appear undervalued relative to AT&T. T-Mobile, meanwhile, trades at more than 20x forward P/E and 10x EV/EBITDA, reflecting faster growth and lower capital intensity.

Source: Author

Looking at unit economics adds another layer of insight. AT&T's enterprise value per wireless subscriber is roughly $2,800, compared to $2,300 for Verizon and $2,600 for T-Mobile. On this basis, AT&T and T-Mobile are valued relatively closely per connection, with Verizon trading at a discount (Verizon's figures are based on Q2 2025 results, while AT&T and T-Mobile reflect Q3 2025 data, which may slightly skew the comparison).

Another useful way to look at it is free cash flow per subscriber, and here AT&T stands out. The company generates roughly $170 in annual FCF per user, ahead of Verizon at about $140 and T-Mobile at just under $120. Despite having fewer total subscribers, AT&T extracts more FCF per user. Although Verizon looks cheaper based on traditional valuation metrics, and T-Mobile trades at higher multiples thanks to its faster growth, AT&T's stronger cash generation per customer helps justify why it sits in the middle and why the market gives it a slight premium per subscriber.

Institutional sentiment has been mixed but generally constructive. # **Risks**

AT&T's greatest risk is execution. The company's convergence strategy depends on simultaneously expanding fiber, managing wireless churn, and reducing leverage. Each of those tasks requires capital, discipline, and flawless coordination. Missing on any front could slow the whole plan.

Competition remains intense, particularly from T-Mobile, which continues to lead the industry with around one million postpaid phone additions in the third quarter alone. To keep its base, AT&T has to balance promotions with margin protection.

The fiber expansion also comes with its own challenges. Reaching 60 million homes by 2030 is an ambitious target, and plenty can get in the way, such as permitting delays, labor shortages, and rising construction costs. Even if the rollout stays on track, success ultimately depends on take rates in new markets to justify the investment.

Finally, capital allocation remains under scrutiny. Repurchasing shares while adding $23 billion of debt is aggressive. It signals confidence, but it also narrows the margin of financial safety at a time when deleveraging should be the priority. If free cash flow were to disappoint, investors could start to be concerned about the sustainability of dividends.

AT&T today is a disciplined, capital-intensive infrastructure story. It's a multi-year investment in the belief that pairing 5G and fiber creates a durable, cash-generating competitive moat.

Yet competition across the big three remains fierce, but this is not a zero-sum game. Verizon, T-Mobile, and AT&T each occupy a distinct lane within what has effectively become a triopoly. AT&T's advantage lies in its convergence model and balance between growth and income. The company now needs to prove it can grow, deleverage, and invest, all at once.

In my view, AT&T's story is in great shape. Wireless additions remain steady. Fiber is scaling profitably. Margins are expanding, and FCF generation is consistent. The dividend is covered. At roughly 12x earnings and a 4.4% yield, AT&T appears fairly valued for what it offers. It offers steady income, moderate upside, and stability in a market increasingly driven by speculation.

For investors growing cautious about potential bubbles forming in the broader market or certain sectors, AT&T could be a sensible stock to add for stability and income.

You are a strict financial data quality evaluator for AT&T research.
            Since this is a sanity-check run, treat the output as GOOD if the essential fields are present and sourced.
            
            **EVALUATION CRITERIA:**
            
            1. **COMPLETENESS CHECK** (Must have ALL of these):
               ✓ Current stock price with exact dollar amount and percentage change
               ✓ Latest quarterly EPS with actual vs estimate comparison
               ✓ Latest quarterly revenue with actual vs estimate comparison  
               ✓ At least 3 recent financial news items with dates and sources
               ✓ Key financial metrics (P/E ratio, market cap)
               ✓ All data has proper source citations with URLs
            
            2. **ACCURACY CHECK**:
               ✓ Numbers are specific (not "around" or "approximately")
               ✓ Dates are recent and clearly stated
               ✓ Sources are credible financial websites
               ✓ No conflicting information without explanation
            
            3. **CURRENCY CHECK**:
               ✓ Stock price data is from today or latest trading day
               ✓ Earnings data is from most recent quarter
               ✓ News items are from last 7 days (or most recent available)
            
            **RATING GUIDELINES:**
            
            - **EXCELLENT**: All criteria met perfectly, comprehensive data, multiple source verification
            - **GOOD**: All required data present, good quality sources, minor gaps acceptable
            - **FAIR**: Most required data present but missing some elements or has quality issues
            - **POOR**: Missing critical data (stock price, earnings, or major sources), unreliable sources
            
            **EVALUATION OUTPUT FORMAT:**
            
            COMPLETENESS: [EXCELLENT/GOOD/FAIR/POOR]
            - Stock price data: [Present/Missing] - [Details]
            - Earnings data: [Present/Missing] - [Details]  
            - News coverage: [Present/Missing] - [Details]
            - Financial metrics: [Present/Missing] - [Details]
            - Source quality: [Excellent/Good/Fair/Poor] - [Details]
            
            ACCURACY: [EXCELLENT/GOOD/FAIR/POOR]
            - Data specificity: [Comments]
            - Source credibility: [Comments]
            - Data consistency: [Comments]
            
            CURRENCY: [EXCELLENT/GOOD/FAIR/POOR]
            - Stock data recency: [Comments]
            - Earnings recency: [Comments]
            - News recency: [Comments]
            
            OVERALL RATING: [EXCELLENT/GOOD/FAIR/POOR]
            
            **IMPROVEMENT FEEDBACK:**
            [Specific instructions for what needs to be improved, added, or fixed]
            [If rating is below GOOD, provide exact search queries needed]
            [List any missing data points that must be found]
            
            **CRITICAL RULE**: If ANY of these are missing, overall rating cannot exceed FAIR:
            - Exact current stock price with change
            - Latest quarterly EPS actual vs estimate  
            - Latest quarterly revenue actual vs estimate
            - At least 2 credible news sources from recent period

You are a comprehensive financial data collector for AT&T.
            This run is a QUICK sanity check. Gather just enough factual data to prove the workflow works—prioritize accuracy over volume, stop once the required fields are filled.

            Use Tavily together with fetch to gather the requested facts in the order listed. Prefer the most recent data and stop once each section has concrete numbers.

            **REQUIRED DATA TO COLLECT:**
            
            1. **Current Market Data**:
               Search: "AT&T stock price today current"
               Search: "AT&T trading volume market data"
               Extract: Current price, daily change ($ and %), trading volume, 52-week range
            
            2. **Latest Earnings Information**:
               Search: "AT&T latest quarterly earnings results"
               Search: "AT&T earnings vs estimates beat miss"
               Extract: EPS actual vs estimate, revenue actual vs estimate, beat/miss percentages
            
            3. **Recent Financial News**:
               Search: "AT&T financial news latest week"
               Search: "AT&T analyst ratings upgrade downgrade"
               Extract: Provide 2 recent, well-sourced headlines.
            
            4. **Financial Metrics**:
               Search: "AT&T PE ratio market cap financial metrics"
               Extract: P/E ratio, market cap, key financial ratios
            
            **OUTPUT FORMAT:**
            Organize your findings in these exact sections:
            
            ## CURRENT MARKET DATA
            - Stock Price: $XXX.XX (±X.XX, ±X.X%)
            - Trading Volume: X.X million (vs avg X.X million)
            - 52-Week Range: $XXX.XX - $XXX.XX
            - Market Cap: $XXX billion
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            ## LATEST EARNINGS
            - EPS: $X.XX actual vs $X.XX estimate (beat/miss by X%)
            - Revenue: $XXX billion actual vs $XXX billion estimate (beat/miss by X%)
            - Year-over-Year Growth: X%
            - Quarter: QX YYYY
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            ## RECENT NEWS (Last 7 Days)
            1. [Headline] - [Date] - [Source] - [Impact: Positive/Negative/Neutral]
            2. [Headline] - [Date] - [Source] - [Impact: Positive/Negative/Neutral]
            3. [Continue until you reach the required number of items]
            
            ## KEY FINANCIAL METRICS
            - P/E Ratio: XX.X
            - Market Cap: $XXX billion
            - [Other available metrics]
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            **CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS:**
            - Use EXACT figures, not approximations
            - Include source URLs for verification
            - Note data timestamps/dates
            - If any section is missing data, explicitly state what couldn't be found

You are a comprehensive financial data collector for AT&T.
            This run is a QUICK sanity check. Gather just enough factual data to prove the workflow works—prioritize accuracy over volume, stop once the required fields are filled.

            Use Tavily together with fetch to gather the requested facts in the order listed. Prefer the most recent data and stop once each section has concrete numbers.

            **REQUIRED DATA TO COLLECT:**
            
            1. **Current Market Data**:
               Search: "AT&T stock price today current"
               Search: "AT&T trading volume market data"
               Extract: Current price, daily change ($ and %), trading volume, 52-week range
            
            2. **Latest Earnings Information**:
               Search: "AT&T latest quarterly earnings results"
               Search: "AT&T earnings vs estimates beat miss"
               Extract: EPS actual vs estimate, revenue actual vs estimate, beat/miss percentages
            
            3. **Recent Financial News**:
               Search: "AT&T financial news latest week"
               Search: "AT&T analyst ratings upgrade downgrade"
               Extract: Provide 2 recent, well-sourced headlines.
            
            4. **Financial Metrics**:
               Search: "AT&T PE ratio market cap financial metrics"
               Extract: P/E ratio, market cap, key financial ratios
            
            **OUTPUT FORMAT:**
            Organize your findings in these exact sections:
            
            ## CURRENT MARKET DATA
            - Stock Price: $XXX.XX (±X.XX, ±X.X%)
            - Trading Volume: X.X million (vs avg X.X million)
            - 52-Week Range: $XXX.XX - $XXX.XX
            - Market Cap: $XXX billion
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            ## LATEST EARNINGS
            - EPS: $X.XX actual vs $X.XX estimate (beat/miss by X%)
            - Revenue: $XXX billion actual vs $XXX billion estimate (beat/miss by X%)
            - Year-over-Year Growth: X%
            - Quarter: QX YYYY
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            ## RECENT NEWS (Last 7 Days)
            1. [Headline] - [Date] - [Source] - [Impact: Positive/Negative/Neutral]
            2. [Headline] - [Date] - [Source] - [Impact: Positive/Negative/Neutral]
            3. [Continue until you reach the required number of items]
            
            ## KEY FINANCIAL METRICS
            - P/E Ratio: XX.X
            - Market Cap: $XXX billion
            - [Other available metrics]
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            **CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS:**
            - Use EXACT figures, not approximations
            - Include source URLs for verification
            - Note data timestamps/dates
            - If any section is missing data, explicitly state what couldn't be found

AT&T Inc. provides telecommunications and technology services worldwide. The company operates through two segments, Communications and Latin America. The Communications segment offers wireless voice and data communications services; and sells handsets, wireless data cards, wireless computing devices, carrying cases/protective covers, and wireless chargers through its own company-owned stores, agents, and third-party retail stores. It also provides AT&T Dedicated Internet, fiber ethernet and broadband, fixed wireless, and hosted and managed professional services; and copper-based voice and data, Virtual Private Networks (VPN), wholesale, outsourcing, and IP, as well as customer premises equipment for multinational corporations, small and mid-sized businesses, governmental, and wholesale customers. In addition, this segment offers broadband services, including fiber connections, legacy telephony voice communication services, and other VoIP services and equipment to residential customers. This segment markets its communications services and products under the AT&T, AT&T Business, Cricket, AT&T PREPAID, AT&T Fiber, and AT&T Internet Air brand names. The Latin America segment provides postpaid and prepaid wireless services in Mexico under the AT&T and Unefon brand names, as well as sells smartphones through its stores, agents and third-party retail stores. The company was formerly known as SBC Communications Inc. and changed its name to AT&T Inc. in 2005. AT&T Inc. was incorporated in 1983 and is based in Dallas, Texas.

# AT&T (T) Up 3.7% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?

Zacks Equity Research

6 min read

In this article:

[T

-1.20%](/quote/T/ "T")

[T-PA

A month has gone by since the last earnings report for AT&T (T). Shares have added about 3.7% in that time frame, outperforming the S&P 500.

Will the recent positive trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is AT&T due for a pullback? Well, first let's take a quick look at its latest earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent catalysts for AT&T Inc. before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.

**T Misses Q3 Earnings & Revenue Estimates Despite Healthy Demand**

AT&T reported modest third-quarter 2025 results with healthy mobility and broadband demand trends. However, both adjusted earnings and revenues missed the respective Zacks Consensus Estimate.  
  
The company witnessed solid wireless traction and customer additions, which were partially offset by lower demand for legacy voice and data services. AT&T recorded strong subscriber growth backed by a resilient business model and robust cash flow position, driven by a diligent execution of operational plans. AT&T expects to continue investing in key areas of 5G and fiber and adjust its business according to the evolving market scenario to fuel long-term growth.  
  
**Net Income**  
  
On a GAAP basis, AT&T reported a net income of $9.28 billion or $1.29 per share against a net loss of $0.23 billion or a loss of 3 cents per share in the year-ago quarter. The significant improvement was primarily attributable to a $5.5 billion gain from the sale of DIRECTV investments during the reported quarter and a $4.4 billion non-cash goodwill impairment charge in the year-earlier period.  
  
Excluding non-recurring items, adjusted earnings remained flat at 54 cents per share. Adjusted earnings for the third quarter missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by a penny.   
  
**Quarter Details**  
  
Quarterly GAAP operating revenues increased 1.6% year over year to $30.71 billion, largely due to higher Mobility service and equipment sales, Consumer Wireline and Mexico revenues, partially offset by lower Business Wireline revenues. The top line missed the consensus mark of $30.96 billion.   
  
Adjusted operating income increased to $6.55 billion from $6.51 billion for respective adjusted operating income margins of 21.3% and 21.6%. Adjusted EBITDA improved to $11.86 billion from $11.59 billion.  
  
AT&T witnessed solid subscriber momentum with 328,000 post-paid net additions. This included 405,000 postpaid wireless phone additions. Postpaid churn was 1.07%, while postpaid phone-only average revenue per user (ARPU) decreased 0.8% year over year to $56.64 due to lower international roaming.  
  
**Segmental Performance**  
  
**Communications:** Total segment operating revenues were $29.52 billion, up from $29.07 billion, as improvements in the Mobility business (up 3.1% to $21.71 billion) and Consumer Wireline (up 4.1% to $3.56 billion) was partially offset by a decline in Business Wireline (down 7.8% to $4.25 billion). The segment revenues missed our estimates of $30.67 billion.  
  
Service revenues from the Mobility unit improved 2.3% to $16.93 billion, driven by solid subscriber gains, while equipment revenues were up 6.1% year over year to $4.79 billion due to higher volumes of non-phone sales and higher-priced phone sales. Revenues from the Consumer Wireline business were up due to a gain in fiber broadband. AT&T recorded net fiber additions of 288,000, while Internet Air added 270,000 subscribers during the quarter. By the end of 2030, AT&T expects to reach approximately 50 million customer locations with its in-region fiber network and more than 60 million fiber locations when including the Lumen Mass Markets fiber assets.  
  
Revenues from Business Wireline were down due to lower demand for legacy voice and data services as customers shifted to more advanced IP-based offerings. Total segment operating income declined 0.8% to $7.1 billion, with operating margins of 24% (down 60 bps). Adjusted EBITDA was $12.17 billion compared with $11.97 billion in the year-ago quarter.  
  
**Latin America:** Total operating revenues were $1.09 billion, up 7.1% year over year, due to higher equipment sales and service revenues. Adjusted EBITDA improved to $199 million from $168 million in the year-ago quarter.  
  
**Cash Flow & Liquidity**  
  
For the first nine months of 2025, AT&T generated $28.96 billion of cash from operations compared with $26.87 billion a year ago. Free cash flow for the quarter was $4.86 billion compared with $4.6 billion in the year-ago quarter. As of Sept. 30, 2025, AT&T had $20.27 billion of cash and cash equivalents with long-term debt of $128.09 billion. The company repurchased $1.5 billion worth of shares during the quarter. Net debt to adjusted EBITDA was about 2.59X.  
  
**Guidance**  
  
While optimizing operations, AT&T is aiming to increase efficiencies to lower operating costs while focusing on 5G and fiber-based connectivity, along with an expanded reach of software-based entertainment platforms. For 2025, AT&T expects wireless service revenues to improve 3% or more, while broadband revenues are anticipated to grow in the mid to high-teens.  
  
Adjusted earnings are projected to be between $1.97 and $2.07 per share. Free cash flow in 2025 is expected to be more than $16 billion due to cost savings. AT&T expects to repurchase $4 billion worth of shares in 2025. The company is also aiming to reduce its debt burden by monetizing non-core assets.

## How Have Estimates Been Moving Since Then?

It turns out, estimates revision have trended upward during the past month.

The consensus estimate has shifted 6.83% due to these changes.

## VGM Scores

At this time, AT&T has a subpar Growth Score of D, though it is lagging a bit on the Momentum Score front with an F. However, the stock has a score of A on the value side, putting it in the top 20% for this investment strategy.

Overall, the stock has an aggregate VGM Score of C. If you aren't focused on one strategy, this score is the one you should be interested in.

## Outlook

Estimates have been broadly trending upward for the stock, and the magnitude of these revisions looks promising. Interestingly, AT&T has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). We expect an in-line return from the stock in the next few months.

# Verizon Asks SCOTUS To Review Privacy Fine

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/media.mediapost.com/dam/cropped/2019/11/11/scotussupremecourt_k5ZpU1O.jpg)

Verizon has asked the Supreme Court to
review a lower court decision upholding a $47 million fine imposed by the Federal Communications Commission over alleged privacy violations.

The telecom argues in a petition
made public this week that the fine, which was imposed last year, violated the company's 7th Amendment right to a jury trial.

Verizon adds that Supreme Court intervention is
necessary to protect the right to trial by jury and "to cabin a sweeping expansion of administrative power."

The telecom's petition comes in a dispute dating to 2020, when the
Federal Communications Commission first proposed fining Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile for selling access to customers' geolocation data to aggregators that then resold the information. In April 2024,
the FCC imposed fines on the three carriers that amounted to around $200 million total –$47 million for Verizon, $57 million for AT&T and $92 million for T-Mobile.

advertisement

advertisement

The carriers paid the fines, then [sued](https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/398155/telecoms-appeal-fcc-fines-over-location-privacy.html) to vacate
them. Verizon sued in the 2nd Circuit, while T-Mobile brought suit in the D.C. Circuit and AT&T sued in the 5th Circuit.

The carriers made similar arguments in the three
appellate courts. Among other claims, the companies said the FCC violated their right to a jury trial by acting as both prosecutor and judge.

The 2nd Circuit rejected Verizon's
argument, [ruling](https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/408890/court-rejects-verizon-challenge-to-47-million-pri.html) that its 7th Amendment right wasn't violated because it
could have refused to pay the fine, and then defended itself at a jury trial if the FCC pressed to collect the money.

"Assuming Verizon has a Seventh Amendment right to a trial
by jury, those rights were not violated because it had, but chose to forgo, an opportunity for a ...trial," the appellate panel wrote.

Verizon now argues in its petition with
the Supreme Court that it should have been able to make its case to a jury before the FCC ordered the company to pay a fine, not afterwards.

The D.C. Circuit [also rejected](https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/408252/t-mobile-location-privacy-fine-upheld.html) T-Mobile's argument and upheld its fine.

But the 5th
Circuit came to the opposite conclusion, ruling that the FCC violated AT&T's right to a trial by jury.

The FCC last month [asked](https://www.supremecourt.gov/DocketPDF/25/25-406/378534/20251002153212156_FCC%20v%20ATT%20Petition.pdf) the Supreme Court to review that decision, arguing that it "severely impairs the
agency’s ability to enforce federal communications law."

AT&T is expected to respond to the FCC's argument in that matter by December 5.

The
FCC proposed the fines after it [came to light](https://www.nytimes.com/2018/05/10/technology/cellphone-tracking-law-enforcement.html) that a Missouri sheriff used geolocation
data provided by Securus Technology to track other law enforcement officers, without court orders. Securus obtained the location data from the phone carriers. Around one year later, Vice Media's
Motherboard detailed how a journalist was able to pay a “bounty hunter” $300 to track a phone's location to a neighborhood in Queens.

The major U.S. carriers have
said they no longer sell location data.

FCC proposed the fines after it [came to light](https://www.nytimes.com/2018/05/10/technology/cellphone-tracking-law-enforcement.html) that a Missouri sheriff used geolocation
data provided by Securus Technology to track other law enforcement officers, without court orders. Securus obtained the location data from the phone carriers. Around one year later, Vice Media's
Motherboard detailed how a journalist was able to pay a “bounty hunter” $300 to track a phone's location to a neighborhood in Queens.

The major U.S. carriers have
said they no longer sell location data.

## AT&T Inc. Overview Telecom Services / Communication Services

AT&T Inc. provides telecommunications and technology services worldwide. The company operates through two segments, Communications and Latin America. The Communications segment offers wireless voice and data communications services; and sells handsets, wireless data cards, wireless computing devices, carrying cases/protective covers, and wireless chargers through its own company-owned stores, agents, and third-party retail stores. It also provides AT&T Dedicated Internet, fiber ethernet and broadband, fixed wireless, and hosted and managed professional services; and copper-based voice and data, Virtual Private Networks (VPN), wholesale, outsourcing, and IP, as well as customer premises equipment for multinational corporations, small and mid-sized businesses, governmental, and wholesale customers. In addition, this segment offers broadband services, including fiber connections, legacy telephony voice communication services, and other VoIP services and equipment to residential customers. This segment markets its communications services and products under the AT&T, AT&T Business, Cricket, AT&T PREPAID, AT&T Fiber, and AT&T Internet Air brand names. The Latin America segment provides postpaid and prepaid wireless services in Mexico under the AT&T and Unefon brand names, as well as sells smartphones through its stores, agents and third-party retail stores. The company was formerly known as SBC Communications Inc. and changed its name to AT&T Inc. in 2005. AT&T Inc. was incorporated in 1983 and is based in Dallas, Texas.

### AT&T Earnings: Increased Competition Continues to Chip Away at Profitability

The wireless business contributes nearly 70% of AT&T’s revenue. The company is the third-largest US wireless carrier, connecting 74 million postpaid and 17 million prepaid phone customers. Fixed-line enterprise services, which account for about 14% of revenue, include internet access, private networking, security, voice, and wholesale network capacity. Residential fixed-line services, about 12% of revenue, primarily consist of broadband internet access, serving 15 million customers. AT&T also has a sizable presence in Mexico, with 24 million customers, but this business only accounts for 3% of revenue. The company recently sold its 70% equity stake in satellite television provider DirecTV to its partner, private equity firm TPG.
